headline: Awami League terror politics exposed by harassment of Dr. Yunus in US
summary: NCP convener Nahid Islam condemned the alleged harassment of Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus at a US airport, calling it a manifestation of Awami League's violent politics. Legal action is promised.
details: NCP convener Nahid Islam has strongly condemned an alleged attempt to harass former interim government chief advisor Professor Dr. Muhammad Yunus at John F. Kennedy International Airport in the United States. He stated that this incident once again exposed the brutal, violent, and inhumane nature of the Awami League's terror-based politics.

In a statement on Tuesday, Nahid Islam commented that the Awami League's "terrorist forces" have not changed their character even two years after being rejected by the people of Bangladesh. He noted a lack of remorse for past misdeeds and called for the complete eradication of this active terrorist network, both domestically and abroad.

Islam further demanded swift trials and execution of sentences for those involved in the "fascist regime's" alleged GUM (forced disappearances) and killings, including the July massacre. He called for legal proceedings against the Awami League as a party for alleged genocide and terrorism.

Recalling the crucial role of Dr. Muhammad Yunus and the interim government members in restoring democracy and rebuilding the economy during the nation's critical juncture, Nahid Islam urged the government to take effective measures to ensure their safety.

headline_marked: [[CUET Vice-Chancellor]] confined for 21 hours amid student protest, claims chest pain
headline: CUET Vice-Chancellor confined for 21 hours amid student protest, claims chest pain
summary: Students locked the gates of the Vice-Chancellor's office, cutting off water and electricity, demanding his resignation. He reported chest pain and requested medical attention.
details: The Vice-Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, has been confined to his office for 21 hours by protesting students. He reported experiencing chest pain and requested to see a doctor and be hospitalized.
Students locked the gates of the VC's office building around 12 PM on Monday, also cutting off the water and electricity supply. This left the VC and at least 11 others trapped inside.
Journalists gained access to the office around 12:30 PM on Tuesday and spoke with the VC. He stated, "My left side is hurting. I want to see a doctor and be hospitalized."

University physician Dr. Md. Shahabuddin examined the VC and reported his pulse and blood pressure were normal. He stated the VC was "uncomfortable" due to being confined but did not require hospitalization.
However, a second doctor, Dr. Tipul Kanti Dey from Raujan Upazila Health Complex, reported the VC's blood pressure as 150/100 and confirmed chest pain. He advised hospitalization.

The protest began on September 22, with students demanding the reinstatement of the previous VC, Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, who was removed on September 21. The new VC, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, was appointed on the same day.
Students have vowed to keep the gates locked until the new VC resigns. "He can leave with dignity once he resigns," said Abidur Rahman, a student representative.
CUET's academic activities, including classes and examinations, have been suspended since the protests began.
caption:
CUET Vice-Chancellor confined for 21 hours by protesting students. He claims chest pain and requests medical attention.

The Vice-Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, has been confined to his office for 21 hours by protesting students. He reported experiencing chest pain and requested to see a doctor and be hospitalized.

Students locked the gates of the VC's office building around 12 PM on Monday, also cutting off the water and electricity supply. This left the VC and at least 11 others trapped inside.

Journalists gained access to the office around 12:30 PM on Tuesday and spoke with the VC. He stated, "My left side is hurting. I want to see a doctor and be hospitalized."

University physician Dr. Md. Shahabuddin examined the VC and reported his pulse and blood pressure were normal. He stated the VC was "uncomfortable" due to being confined but did not require hospitalization.

However, a second doctor, Dr. Tipul Kanti Dey from Raujan Upazila Health Complex, reported the VC's blood pressure as 150/100 and confirmed chest pain. He advised hospitalization.

The protest began on September 22, with students demanding the reinstatement of the previous VC, Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, who was removed on September 21. The new VC, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, was appointed on the same day.

Students have vowed to keep the gates locked until the new VC resigns. "He can leave with dignity once he resigns," said Abidur Rahman, a student representative.

CUET's academic activities, including classes and examinations, have been suspended since the protests began.
